/TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Issued at 246 PM MDT Sat Sep 26 2026

A trough is favored to be trekking across the Southern and Central 
United States Tuesday morning, with an active jet streak to the 
north. A cold front is forecast to come through the area sometime 
during the morning and afternoon. LREF standard deviation in wind 
direction shows large amounts of spread south and east of a line 
from Cheyenne Wells, CO to Stratton, NE around noon. This would 
indicate that the cold front would be along or southeast of this 
line as well. High temperatures are currently forecast in the low to 
mid 70s across the forecast area. Precipitation appears likely along 
the front, as NBM 24 hr precipitation guidance suggests that most of 
the area has greater than a 50% chance of receiving greater than 0.1 
inches of rain, with portions of Gove and Graham Counties in Kansas 
around an 80% chance. The only area at less than 50% is portions of 
Yuma County in Colorado and far northwest Dundy County in Nebraska. 
LREF guidance shows all areas having less than a 25% chance of 
seeing surface CAPE (a measure of atmospheric instability) greater 
than 1000 J/kg Tuesday afternoon and evening, which would suggest 
that this precipitation would be linked to widespread rain as 
opposed to convective thunderstorms. The exception to this would be 
if the cold front can manage to come through during the later 
afternoon or evening. NBM 75th percentile and higher solutions show 
temperatures in the upper 70s or higher for highs, which could 
correspond with this scenario. This would allow for extra 
instability and a higher chance for thunderstorms to develop. 
However, this is not the favored solution, as rain is primarily 
expected to exist ahead of the cold front, which would minimize 
temperatures and prevent more significant instability. 

Cool and wet conditions are expected to continue going into 
Wednesday in association with the trough approaching from the west. 
Uncertainty continues to remain as to how fast this feature will 
move eastward. Ensembles show the trough centered in one of the 4-
Corners States with a large amount of spread on the trailing edge, 
which would indicate a slower progression. Guidance also continues 
to show a modest 40-50 kt jet streak curved cyclonically around the 
base of the trough, which would favor a surface low developing in 
the Southern High Plains. Ensemble and deterministic guidance 
indicates this surface low may be very slow moving, and perhaps 
stationary Wednesday and Thursday in association with the slow-
moving trough. This would create the potential for several days of 
precipitation. NBM 24 hr precipitation guidance shows most of the 
area higher than a 70% chance for greater than 0.1 inches of rain 
Wednesday, with a 40-45% chance on Thursday. Additionally, higher 
end (90th percentile and higher) 48 hr precipitation scenarios show 
between 3 and 4 inches of rain between Wednesday and Thursday. This 
is a low confidence scenario (5%), but could lead to some localized 
flash flooding if it occurs. 

It should also be noted that the surface low may deepen enough to 
where northerly winds sustained at 15-20 kts are possible Wednesday 
and Thursday afternoon, particularly across portions of Eastern 
Colorado and far Western Counties in Kansas where NBM guidance shows 
a 40% chance or greater for such a solution. While highs are 
currently forecast in the upper 60s to lower 70s, we may see a broad 
area of highs in the low to mid 60s due to the strong northerly 
winds and rain. NBM guidance suggests about a 15-30% chance across 
most of the forecast area that highs are below 65 F. 

Model guidance begins to diverge by Friday morning, as ensembles are 
inconsistent on whether the trough will be through the area or not. 
If the trough remains in the area, conditions similar to Wednesday 
and Thursday could be experienced. However, if the trough is through 
the area, warm and dry conditions are possible. An active jet streak 
to the north may also introduce a more active weather pattern to the 
forecast area, with EC and LREF ensemble 500-mb mean heights showing 
a northwesterly flow coming into the forecast area. This would 
suggest the potential for meandering temperatures as well as on and 
off precipitation with shortwave systems.
